haiku-low.q1: On-call runs the single failover command; that starts it. Detection is automatic but only pages on-call. Nothing is promoted automatically.
haiku-low.q2: The command stops with nothing changed, unless on-call gives an explicit accept-data-loss override, which is logged.
haiku-low.q3: Before B's database is promoted: A's lease has expired plus clock-skew margin, and the witness compare-and-set succeeded. Before B's workers start: promotion is done. Before DNS moves: B's health check, including a test write, passes at full size.
haiku-low.q4: Sessions live in Redis, which is not replicated. Users signed in at failover must sign in again. This is accepted.
haiku-low.q5: It is never primary again. A is rebuilt as a replica of B, and its old volume is kept for manual reconciliation. Nothing merges automatically.
haiku-low.q6: A's local fencing agent makes A read-only or stops it once renewals fail beyond lease length minus margin. B waits for lease expiry plus clock-skew margin before promoting.
haiku-low.q7: The witness store, a record outside both regions. The failover command writes it by compare-and-set. A's primary renews its lease in it and compares its epoch and timeline with it. A's fencing agent reads it on return.
haiku-low.q8: Jobs A marked running are requeued at promotion. On B, a dead worker's lock lapses and the reaper requeues the job, until max attempts, then it is failed and paged. Requeue is safe only once idempotency keys are built.
haiku-low.q9: If the DNS health check fails, fix B and resume from that check. Resuming after other partway failures is NOT STATED. Returning to A is NOT STATED beyond a separate planned switchover; A's old database is never primary again.
haiku-low.q10: NOT STATED for the experience during failover. Cached clients keep reaching A until the 60 s TTL expires. Some resolvers ignore TTL, so those users arrive later.
haiku-low.q11: Target RPO is 30 s. Loss is limited by the replay-lag gate of 30 s or less and an LSN gap check. Changes A committed but never sent to B can still be lost. The byte threshold is not yet set.

sonnet.q1: A failover is started only when on-call runs the single failover command. Detection (3 probes, 2 of 3 seeing 3 consecutive failures) only pages on-call; nothing is promoted automatically.
sonnet.q2: If lag is over 30 s or the LSN gap is over the byte threshold, the command stops with nothing changed, unless the operator gives an explicit accept-data-loss override. An override is logged with the lag and LSN gap, and the failover then continues.
sonnet.q3: Before promoting B's database: A's lease must have expired (plus clock-skew margin), and the witness compare-and-set must have succeeded (active=B, epoch n+1). Before B's workers start: B's database is promoted, the endpoint repointed and running jobs requeued. Before DNS moves: B's health check must pass, including a test write.
sonnet.q4: Sessions are in Redis, which is not replicated between regions, so they are not copied. Users must sign in again. This is accepted.
sonnet.q5: It is never primary again. A's fencing agent refuses to start it as primary if the witness epoch is higher. A is rebuilt as a replica of B, by a fresh base backup or pg_rewind if its conditions are met. Changes A made after the histories split are discarded. The old volume is kept for manual reconciliation and nothing is merged automatically. Returning to A is a separate planned switchover.
sonnet.q6: A's own local fencing agent, lease-based. If lease renewals to the witness fail for longer than the lease length minus a safety margin, it makes A's database read-only or stops it. B waits for the lease to expire plus clock skew before promoting. Residual risk: if the agent hangs while A's database stays writable, nothing can stop it.
sonnet.q7: The witness store in a third location holds the record (active_region, epoch, lease_holder, lease_expiry, Postgres timeline). The failover command reads it and writes it by compare-and-set. A's primary renews the lease in it, and A's fencing agent reads it, including when A returns. An old primary compares its epoch and timeline with the record.
sonnet.q8: Failover does not wait for A's workers. Jobs that B's copy shows as running are requeued in step 3. Jobs A finished after the last change that reached B show as unfinished on B and are run again. Workers still alive on A may finish external work, but their database writes fail and are discarded. Requeuing is safe only if external side effects are idempotent, keyed by job and step, and that is not yet built.
sonnet.q9: If B's health check fails, DNS is not moved. The team fixes B and resumes from that health check. Other failures before promotion abort with nothing changed or promoted. NOT STATED: how the run resumes after a failure at other steps, and any conditions for going back to A. A's old database is never primary again, and moving back is a separate planned switchover.
sonnet.q10: NOT STATED for a client with cached DNS pointing at A. The document says only that the TTL is 60 s, that some resolvers ignore TTL so some users arrive later, and that A is fenced read-only or stopped.
sonnet.q11: The RPO is 30 s. The gate limits it: replay lag must be 30 s or less and the LSN gap under a byte threshold, or else an explicit override is needed. Lag cannot show changes A committed but never sent to B, so a large LSN gap can mean loss even when lag is under 30 s. The byte threshold is not yet set. Measuring the gap needs A's latest log position, and the source for that is an open item.
